title: Building – Construction of a Retaining Structure Existing Without a Permit August 2014
description: Property owners built a retaining structure on a riverbank lot without a permit, in an area with a history of bank subsidence. The municipality ordered the dwelling vacated.

refusal.basis: analogous: order appeal in which the order itself states the submitted information is inadequate; the panel found permit application requirements unmet

outcome_summary: The evacuation directive was removed (no imminent danger per the appellants' engineer) and replaced with barriers. The permit information requirements remain, with a reasonable time to comply.

quotes.text: The information provided is inadequate to confirm compliance with the Alberta Building Code requirements. Please provide a detailed slope stability study prepared by a qualified geotechnical engineer.

The order required a qualified geotechnical engineer's slope stability study, peer review by a consultant familiar with the site, geotechnical on-site review, and in-situ testing and drawings by a qualified structural engineer. The panel accepted the appellants' engineering company evidence on imminent danger and repairability.
